title: The Joint Attack and the Green Leaves

blocks.text: Before the battle opens, Dina Beg proposes a joint morning attack so his troops and the Khalsa can strike the Pathans together. The Singhs bluntly warn him that once the fighting begins they will cut down whoever stands before them and will not pause to distinguish friend from foe.

To prevent confusion, Dina Beg orders his own soldiers to wear green leaves on their headgear as a visible sign for the Sikh warriors. With that precaution settled, the hostile line is surveyed and the enemy is described in formal deployment, with artillery in the front and musketeers on both flanks.

Even so, the Nawab remains anxious when the Khalsa does not appear at the exact moment he expects. The page therefore joins tactical planning to battlefield tension, showing how the alliance depends on Sikh timing, Sikh confidence, and clear signals amid the chaos.
